pipeline: 6 public seaborn tables (titanic, mpg, tips, car_crashes, planets, healthexp) -> data tabular (1800 verified examples) -> tinyforge worker run backend=soup, NF4, 200 steps, batch 1 x accum 2, 9m29s, 2 examples/step -> adapter -> GGUF (llama.cpp b11380: adapter f16, base Q4_K_M) -> llama-server -ngl 24 on RTX 3050 Ti 4 GB, ~18 tok/s -> eval on 100 questions about an UNSEEN table (penguins)
caveats: tuned = 100/100 is a ceiling; base_instructed is already 93%, so this test cannot show how much headroom fine-tuning adds
all 7 base misses are the same malformed MAX/MIN call (MAX bill_length_mm without parentheses): the gain here is consistency, not new capability
test questions use the same 12 templates as training on a new schema, so it measures transfer to new tables, not to new kinds of questions
adapter trained on the NF4 base, served on a Q4_K_M base: a small quantisation mismatch that did not hurt here
n=100, one run, greedy decoding, no confidence interval; the same test on the 3B model was not run
